answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may place orders. The protocol limits each account’s influence to its bonded amount and slashes stake when fraud is proven, so splitting funds across a garden of fake agents does not create extra voting or trading power. An attacker must tie up real capital for each identity and risks losing it; the glacier-like delay before withdrawal makes rapid identity cycling costly, while a ledge of minimum stake keeps tiny accounts out.
